title: India's Foreign Exchange Reserves
plainSummary: India's foreign exchange reserves stand at about ₹69.8 lakh crore, up ₹1.40 lakh crore over the week. Reserves cushion the rupee and pay for imports; most of it sits in foreign currencies, the rest in gold, SDRs and the IMF.

metrics.label: Total Reserves
metrics.plain: India's total war-chest of foreign assets — what backs the rupee and pays for imports.

metrics.label: Foreign Currency Assets
metrics.plain: Foreign currencies the RBI holds (dollars, euros, etc.) — the bulk of the reserves.

metrics.label: Gold
metrics.plain: Gold held as reserve; rises in value when gold prices climb.

metrics.label: SDRs
metrics.plain: Special Drawing Rights — an IMF reserve asset India can draw on.

metrics.label: Reserve Position in the IMF
metrics.plain: India's automatic drawing quota at the IMF.

provenance.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Weekly Statistical Supplement
provenance.note: Latest 'Foreign Exchange Reserves' table from the WSS (₹ crore column). ~1 week reporting lag.
